title: Wildlife Tourism in Rajasthan: Ranthambore, Sariska, Leopards and Birds
seoTitle: Wildlife Tourism in Rajasthan: Parks, Leopards & Birds | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Plan a wildlife trip in Rajasthan: Ranthambore and Sariska tigers, Jhalana and Jawai leopards, Keoladeo's birds, the Desert National Park and the Chambal.
description: A guide to wildlife tourism in Rajasthan: the tiger reserves of Ranthambore, Sariska and Mukundra Hills, leopards at Jhalana and Jawai, winter birds at Keoladeo and Khichan, the great Indian bustard in the Desert National Park, gharials on the Chambal, blackbuck at Tal Chhapar, seasons and a sample route.
dek: Rajasthan is not only forts and desert. It has tigers among ruined palaces, leopards on granite hills, and some of India's best winter birding.

hero.alt: The tigress known as Machli resting on open ground in Ranthambore National Park

intro: Rajasthan has five tiger reserves: Ranthambore, Sariska, Mukundra Hills, Ramgarh Vishdhari and Dhaulpur-Karauli. Ranthambore is one of India's most visited parks, and Sariska is the closest tiger reserve to Delhi.

Beyond tigers, the state has leopards living near people at Jhalana and Jawai, a world-famous bird wetland at Keoladeo, desert wildlife such as the critically endangered great Indian bustard, and gharials and dolphins on the Chambal river. Most of it fits easily into a trip around Jaipur, Udaipur or Jodhpur.
quickAnswer: The main wildlife destinations in Rajasthan are Ranthambore and Sariska for tigers, Jhalana (Jaipur) and Jawai for leopards, Keoladeo National Park in Bharatpur for winter birds, the Desert National Park near Jaisalmer for the great Indian bustard, and the National Chambal Sanctuary for gharials. October to March is the most comfortable season; tiger sightings often improve from April to June.
takeaways: Rajasthan has five tiger reserves; Ranthambore and Sariska are the most visited.
Jhalana and Jawai are among India's best places to see leopards.
Keoladeo is a UNESCO site and a national park, best from November to February.
Tiger reserve cores close from 1 July to 30 September.
Winter is best for birds and comfort; summer for tiger sightings.

rows: Hills and farmland, not a national park

items.name: Ranthambore
body: Tigers in dry forest around lakes and a 10th-century fort. Zones are allotted by the booking system; book early for winter weekends.

image.alt: Ranthambore Fort on a ridge above the forest of Ranthambore National Park
image.caption: Ranthambore Fort and forest

items.name: Sariska
body: About four hours from Delhi, with tigers brought from Ranthambore and heritage inside the reserve.

items.name: Leopards at Jhalana and Jawai
body: Jhalana offers safaris inside Jaipur; Jawai's leopards live on granite hills near villages.

items.name: Keoladeo and Khichan
body: Keoladeo for ducks, storks and raptors; Khichan village near Phalodi for thousands of demoiselle cranes in winter.

items.name: The desert and the Chambal
body: The Desert National Park for bustards, sandgrouse and chinkara; the Chambal for boat trips among gharials.

sections.heading: Where to stay
list: Ranthambore: lodges and resorts along the Ranthambore road in Sawai Madhopur, from simple hotels to luxury camps.
Sariska: hotels near Sariska gate, or heritage palaces in the Alwar area.
Jawai: a small number of lodges and tented camps among the hills; book early for winter.
Bharatpur: guesthouses and hotels close to the Keoladeo gate, useful for dawn starts.
Jaisalmer: stay in town or in desert camps for the Desert National Park.

sections.heading: Tips for wildlife in Rajasthan
list: Book Ranthambore permits as early as possible for October to March weekends and holidays.
Pair wildlife with heritage: Ranthambore fort, Kumbhalgarh's walls near Jawai, or Bhangarh near Sariska.
Visit Keoladeo early in the morning, when birds are most active and the light is soft.
Keep clear of great Indian bustard breeding areas and follow guides' instructions in the desert.

rows: Comfortable; birds at Keoladeo and Khichan

safety: Sightings are never guaranteed; plan several drives and enjoy the forest itself.
Stay in the vehicle on safaris and follow your guide.
Book permits only through official forest department portals or trusted operators.
Never feed animals or leave litter in a park.
Carry water and sun protection; Rajasthan's summer heat is intense.

faqs.q: Which is the best wildlife sanctuary in Rajasthan?
faqs.a: Ranthambore National Park is the best known for tigers; Keoladeo for birds and Jawai for leopards.

faqs.q: How many tiger reserves are there in Rajasthan?
faqs.a: Five: Ranthambore, Sariska, Mukundra Hills, Ramgarh Vishdhari and Dhaulpur-Karauli.
Core zones close from 1 July to 30 September.

faqs.q: Where can I see leopards in Rajasthan?
faqs.a: At Jhalana in Jaipur and at Jawai in Pali district.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Ranthambore?
faqs.a: Two nights with three or four drives is a good minimum; add a night in Jaipur or Bharatpur for leopards or birds.

faqs.q: Where can I see the great Indian bustard?
faqs.a: In the Desert National Park near Jaisalmer, though the bird is critically endangered and rarely seen.
